limitations: Read-only review with Read/Glob/Grep only: I verified the recorded commands, exit codes, durations, rustc/cargo provenance and cargo-test stdout inside the check artifacts and read the committed corpora, but I did not execute cargo, Zod, AJV, Node or Python, and I could not recompute the reviewed tree hash 07efd896… or the checks hash 0fa1400c… myself.

Without git access I could not diff against the pre-change or attempt-02 state. That the only policy-relevant source change is the `unit`/bypass reordering rests on reading the current code against the attempt-02 finding text plus the new unit test, not on a diff.

contracts/compatibility/g25/{cases,outcomes}.json are single-line artifacts, so ripgrep counting is line-based. The 15,658 case/outcome totals, the 46 roots and the residual-strictness breakdown come from the recorded tool stdout and the generated report, which are themselves digest-bound to the committed bytes; I did not enumerate per-case outcomes.

Scored chunk `validation-policy` only (validation.rs and its tests, red_team_dataplane.py selection, g25-oracle.mts, g25_report.py/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md, test_g25_generation.py, check-rust/test_ci pins). I did not score the typed-projection decoder internals or the review/CI governance tooling beyond where they supply this chunk's evidence, and phase-20 scope (minimal/default/all, package/export probes, registry, tag and terminal 49-job CI receipts) was not assessed.

Independence of the response expectations still rests on real Zod/AJV execution over schemas whose relaxation is hand-mirrored from the Rust policy in three places (tools/schema-oracle.mts, tools/g25-oracle.mts:19-66, tools/make-red-team-fixtures.mjs). The mirrors are engine-independent, now self-describing in the committed artifact, and guarded by executable self-checks, but they are not derived from the Rust source, so a shared misreading of the policy would not be caught by the corpora alone.

The mutation corpus traverses the strict vendor response trees (tools/g25_fixtures.py:30-66), so paths that exist only in the frozen TypeScript baseline receive no mutation cases. Base-witness acceptance evidence (no `base` case in the residual counts) bounds the practical risk, but TypeScript-only field constraints are exercised only through those base witnesses.

Live service acceptance is unverified and not claimed: the 17 reported airs-cli-rs loopback failures on the `worf` checkout remain unexecuted here, as docs/G25_COMPATIBILITY.md:197 states. Per instructions I read no credential or tenant-registration files and performed no network calls.
